messages.subject: Re: Following adaptation for sampler other than RW
messages.subject_clean: Following adaptation for sampler other than RW
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I have been trying to follow Daniel's suggestion of changing sampling order and I managed implementing these changes although results are mixed for now, but I still have many options to test concerning that (which nodes to resample, how many times should node be resampled...).However I had a question on how nimble worked and I wanted to be sure I was doing nothing wrong.
Let's say I have 5 nodes A to E as in the graphs attach (it is a large simplification of a life cycle model with over 40 000 stochastic nodes)
Node A, B, D are stochastic nodes while C and E are deterministic. C is calculated directly with the value of A and B. E depends on C and D.
B is well mixed because its prior is very informative so its posterior distribution match very closely the prior.
A and D are however poorly mixed compared to B and I wanted to improve model efficiency (in effective size/runtime). So instead of the default sample order (A,B,D), I wanted to try something like (A,B,D,A,B) so that each time D is sampled once, A and B are sampled twice, which should be increasing their effective sample size.
I was wondering, between sampling of A and D, are the deterministic nodes updated? i.e., when the model samples variable D, is the value of node C updated according to the values in A ?
Thanks in advance,
Cheers,
Rémi

On Thursday, August 13, 2020 at 8:38:56 PM UTC+2 remi....@gmail.com wrote:
> Wonderful, thank you very much for your help!
> This may be quite rewardful in the end. I'll most definitely try that solution.
>
> On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 7:26 PM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
> > Yes.  Use the method (for example):
> > conf$setSamplerExecutionOrder( c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) )
> > or just as well:
> > conf$setSamplerExecutionOrder( c(1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 4, 1, 5) )
> >
> > Also, then afterwards, you might find useful:
> > conf$printSamplers(executionOrder = TRUE)
> >
> >
> >
> > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 2:19 PM Rémi Patin <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Thanks a lot for the answer, that helps a lot.
> > >
> > > 1. Thank you, I will look into that to test it. Indeed that may be a niche issue to track acceptance without adaptation so I totally understand the choice.
> > > I always thought that the model kept proposing a new sample until it was accepted before updating the other node so that's a great thing to know it is not the case! Thanks for highlighting the possibility to look into the posterior, I won't use it because I use thinning but that's good to know for the future.
> > >
> > > 2. Thanks for pointing me that idea, I will definitely want to try that.
> > >
> > > 3. If I understood correctly, at each iteration all nodes are updated but for some of them (56% based on the targeted 0.44 acceptance rate) the value stays the same because the proposal is refused. Is it possible to force more update on one node while other nodes are updated less frequently ? e.g. if node A is highly autocorrelated and have a poor mixing while node B has a good mixing, I would want node A to have a lower acceptance of proposal (therefore less autocorrelated) but to update until one proposal is accepted, before updating node B, so it would spare unneeded calculations on the update of node B, before node A finds a good proposal.
> > >
> > > Cheers,
> > > Rémi
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > Le 13/08/2020 à 19:07, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > > To answer your questions:
> > > >
> > > > 1. At present, when you specify adaptive=FALSE (thereby using a fixed proposal scale), the RW sampler doesn't record when / how often / the proportion of transitions (the acceptance rate).  And I'm hesitant to slow it down by tracking this, when it's non-adaptive.  That said, you could easily grab the code form GitHub
> > > > https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/devel/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R#L165
> > > > And modify it so that it still tracks this information even when adaptive=FALSE, but merely doesn't change the scale.  This could be done as easily as removing the one line:
> > > > scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > > > I'll put this modified code, below, and you would only have to remove the RW samplers that are assigned, and add (using conf$addSampler) the new "RW2" sampler, defined below.  To use this sampler, you would need to leave the default of adaptive=TRUE, and also set this nimble system option nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE).
> > > >
> > > > Another option would be for you to use the posterior samples calculate the RW acceptance rate, based on the proportion of times it successfully transitions (e.g., the parameter changes value).
> > > >
> > > > 2. About the target acceptance rate, right now it's hard-coded into the RW sampler at 0.44.  You can also change this in the code below, if you wish.  Or, if it's useful to you, I'm happy to change this into a (user-modifiable) "control list argument", with default value 0.44.  It would be a straightforward change to make, and could go into our next upcoming release (in a couple weeks).  Let me know if that sounds helpful.
> > > >
> > > > Cheers,
> > > > Daniel
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > sampler_RW2 <- nimbleFunction(
> > > >     name = 'sampler_RW2',
> > > >     contains = sampler_BASE,
> > > >     setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
> > > >         ## control list extraction
> > > >         logScale            <- if(!is.null(control$log))                 control$log                 else FALSE
> > > >         reflective          <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))          control$reflective          else FALSE
> > > >         adaptive            <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))            control$adaptive            else TRUE
> > > >         adaptInterval       <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval))       control$adaptInterval       else 200
> > > >         adaptFactorExponent <- if(!is.null(control$adaptFactorExponent)) control$adaptFactorExponent else 0.8
> > > >         scale               <- if(!is.null(control$scale))               control$scale               else 1
> > > >         ## node list generation
> > > >         targetAsScalar <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
> > > >         calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
> > > >         calcNodesNoSelf <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE)
> > > >         isStochCalcNodesNoSelf <- model$isStoch(calcNodesNoSelf)   ## should be made faster
> > > >         calcNodesNoSelfDeterm <- calcNodesNoSelf[!isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > > >         calcNodesNoSelfStoch <- calcNodesNoSelf[isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > > >         ## numeric value generation
> > > >         scaleOriginal <- scale
> > > >         timesRan      <- 0
> > > >         timesAccepted <- 0
> > > >         timesAdapted  <- 0
> > > >         scaleHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > > >         acceptanceHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > > >         if(nimbleOptions('MCMCsaveHistory')) {
> > > >             saveMCMChistory <- TRUE
> > > >         } else saveMCMChistory <- FALSE
> > > >         optimalAR     <- 0.44
> > > >         gamma1        <- 0
> > > >         ## checks
> > > >         if(length(targetAsScalar) > 1)   stop('cannot use RW sampler on more than one target; try RW_block sampler')
> > > >         if(model$isDiscrete(target))     stop('cannot use RW sampler on discrete-valued target; try slice sampler')
> > > >         if(logScale & reflective)        stop('cannot use reflective RW sampler on a log scale (i.e. with options log=TRUE and reflective=TRUE')
> > > >         if(adaptFactorExponent < 0)      stop('cannot use RW sampler with adaptFactorExponent control parameter less than 0')
> > > >         if(scale < 0)                    stop('cannot use RW sampler with scale control parameter less than 0')
> > > >     },
> > > >     run = function() {
> > > >         currentValue <- model[[target]]
> > > >         propLogScale <- 0
> > > >         if(logScale) { propLogScale <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = scale)
> > > >                        propValue <- currentValue * exp(propLogScale)
> > > >         } else         propValue <- rnorm(1, mean = currentValue,  sd = scale)
> > > >         if(reflective) {
> > > >             lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> > > >             upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> > > >             while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
> > > >                 if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
> > > >                 if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
> > > >             }
> > > >         }
> > > >         model[[target]] <<- propValue
> > > >         logMHR <- calculateDiff(model, target)
> > > >         if(logMHR == -Inf) {
> > > >             nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > >             ## Drawing a random number is needed during first testing
> > > >             ## of this step in order to keep the random numbers identical
> > > >             ## to old behavior to see if tests that depend on particular
> > > >             ## sample sequences pass.  Rather than calling runif(1, 0, 1) here,
> > > >             ## we call decide() to ensure same behavior.
> > > >             ## jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > > >             ## When new behavior is acceptable, we can remove the above line
> > > >             ## and uncomment the following:
> > > >             jump <- FALSE
> > > >         } else {
> > > >             logMHR <- logMHR + calculateDiff(model, calcNodesNoSelf) + propLogScale
> > > >             jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > > >             if(jump) {
> > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > > >             } else {
> > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > > >             }
> > > >         }
> > > >         if(adaptive)     adaptiveProcedure(jump)
> > > >     },
> > > >     methods = list(
> > > >         adaptiveProcedure = function(jump = logical()) {
> > > >             timesRan <<- timesRan + 1
> > > >             if(jump)     timesAccepted <<- timesAccepted + 1
> > > >             if(timesRan %% adaptInterval == 0) {
> > > >                 acceptanceRate <- timesAccepted / timesRan
> > > >                 timesAdapted <<- timesAdapted + 1
> > > >                 if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > >                     setSize(scaleHistory, timesAdapted)                 ## scaleHistory
> > > >                     scaleHistory[timesAdapted] <<- scale                ## scaleHistory
> > > >                     setSize(acceptanceHistory, timesAdapted)            ## scaleHistory
> > > >                     acceptanceHistory[timesAdapted] <<- acceptanceRate  ## scaleHistory
> > > >                 }
> > > >                 gamma1 <<- 1/((timesAdapted + 3)^adaptFactorExponent)
> > > >                 gamma2 <- 10 * gamma1
> > > >                 adaptFactor <- exp(gamma2 * (acceptanceRate - optimalAR))
> > > >                 ######scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > > >                 ## If there are upper and lower bounds, enforce a maximum scale of
> > > >                 ## 0.5 * (upper-lower).  This is arbitrary but reasonable.
> > > >                 ## Otherwise, for a poorly-informed posterior,
> > > >                 ## the scale could grow without bound to try to reduce
> > > >                 ## acceptance probability.  This creates enormous cost of
> > > >                 ## reflections.
> > > >                 if(reflective) {
> > > >                     lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> > > >                     upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> > > >                     if(scale >= 0.5*(upper-lower)) {
> > > >                         scale <<- 0.5*(upper-lower)
> > > >                     }
> > > >                 }
> > > >                 timesRan <<- 0
> > > >                 timesAccepted <<- 0
> > > >             }
> > > >         },
> > > >         getScaleHistory = function() {       ## scaleHistory
> > > >             returnType(double(1))
> > > >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > >                 return(scaleHistory)
> > > >             } else {
> > > >                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
> > > >                 return(numeric(1, 0))
> > > >             }
> > > >         },
> > > >         getAcceptanceHistory = function() {  ## scaleHistory
> > > >             returnType(double(1))
> > > >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > >                 return(acceptanceHistory)
> > > >             } else {
> > > >                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
> > > >                 return(numeric(1, 0))
> > > >             }
> > > >         },
> > > >         ##getScaleHistoryExpanded = function() {                                                 ## scaleHistory
> > > >         ##    scaleHistoryExpanded <- numeric(timesAdapted*adaptInterval, init=FALSE)            ## scaleHistory
> > > >         ##    for(iTA in 1:timesAdapted)                                                         ## scaleHistory
> > > >         ##        for(j in 1:adaptInterval)                                                      ## scaleHistory
> > > >         ##            scaleHistoryExpanded[(iTA-1)*adaptInterval+j] <- scaleHistory[iTA]         ## scaleHistory
> > > >         ##    returnType(double(1)); return(scaleHistoryExpanded) },                             ## scaleHistory
> > > >         reset = function() {
> > > >             scale <<- scaleOriginal
> > > >             timesRan      <<- 0
> > > >             timesAccepted <<- 0
> > > >             timesAdapted  <<- 0
> > > >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > >                 scaleHistory  <<- c(0, 0)    ## scaleHistory
> > > >                 acceptanceHistory  <<- c(0, 0)
> > > >             }
> > > >             gamma1 <<- 0
> > > >         }
> > > >     )
> > > > )
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 12:56 PM Rémi Patin <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > I meant tracking the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler. Which from what I understood is still meaningful without adaptation for a sampler. Although it may be relatively constant, I would be interested by its level.
> > > > >
> > > > > However, I am also interested if you can make the RW sampler to tune itself towards another acceptance rate (right now it tunes toward something like 0.4 if I'm not mistaken)
> > > > >
> > > > > Le 13/08/2020 à 18:40, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > > > > Thanks for following up, Rémi.   One question, when you say "would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate?", by the phrase "follow the acceptance rate", do you mean that the RW sampler itself tunes itself towards some "optimal" acceptance rate?  Or, do you mean for you to track (follow) the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler?
> > > > > >
> > > > > > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 10:40 AM remi....@gmail.com <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > Hi All,
> > > > > > > Just a quick follow-up on the different solution I tested following Perry and Daniel advices:
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > - For following the adaptation phase of the slice sampler, I tested the manual solution of stopping the mcmc every 200 runs but it is quite time consuming to run through numerous samplers each time to get the `width` (it is still running in fact). I may test at some point the implementation I proposed in the dev version of nimble, but did not have time for it yet.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > - I also did some test by fixing the scale of the different RW samplers involved in the problematic nodes. Nothing conclusive for now. But I was wondering if it would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate  ?
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > Rémi
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Friday, July 31, 2020 at 5:04:21 PM UTC+2 pdevalpine wrote:
> > > > > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Sure that makes sense.  You could write a for loop to iterate over samplers for many nodes to set the proposal scale and turn the adapt flag FALSE for each one.  I suggested it because it sounded like you were conjecturing that the adaptation has not resulted in proposal scales that you think are most efficient.  (We usually think of efficiency in terms of (effective sample size) / computation time.  The computation time shouldn't change much or at all for different proposal scales, but the effective sample sizes almost certainly will.)  That is possible.  If you increase proposal scale, it may or may not increase effective sample size.  If it does, then fewer iterations would be needed.  I hope that helps.  Let us know if you get interesting results.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > -Perry
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 7:48 AM Rémi PATIN <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Hi Perry,
> > > > > > > > > Thank you for the suggestion and the explanations to do it, I will give it a try. I am however a bit afraid to fix the RW proposal scale, because it concerns around ~2000 nodes. So I am not sure whether a single (or even a few) scale for all the nodes could do the trick.
> > > > > > > > > I suppose if I manually fix the scale to higher value than produced by the adaptation phase, acceptation rate for those nodes will drop leading to slower iteration through those nodes. Meanwhile the samples should be less autocorrelated and less iterations would be needed ?
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Concerning initial values, the model should have relatively good ones for most nodes. I know they have already worked on that and I think that we are currently using older model outputs to initiate the nodes in question. But I will keep that in mind, this could still be problematic.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > > > Rémi
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Le vendredi 31 juillet 2020 16:18:06 UTC+2, pdevalpine a écrit :
> > > > > > > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > If you think the RW proposal scale has adapted to a value that is too small, I can give three suggestions for exploring the issue.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > 1. At the stage of the MCMC configuration (after configureMCMC) but before building the MCMC (before buildMCMC), find the relevant sampler by inspection of mcmcConf$printSamplers() or mcmcConf$getSamplers().  (Here mcmcConf is the object returned by configureMCMC).  Then modify the control list of that sampler to have adapt=FALSE and scale=<your choice>.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > 2. You can make the same settings by modifying the MCMC (after buildMCMC).  If you do it in the uncompiled version (before compileNimble), you can modify mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$scale and mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$adapt, where mcmc is the uncompiled MCMC.  Those values will then be copied to the compiled version to initialize it during compileNimble.  If you want to do it after compileNimble (with say Cmcmc instead of mcmc, where Cmcmc is the compiled version), you will need the same nimbleOptions setting Daniel provided.  You may want to do it this way because you could run it for a while, look at the scale value, then manually adjust it and continue running (with reset = FALSE) to experiment.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > 3. Sometimes providing good initial values can improve the outcome of the RW adaptation.  If the initial values are far from the main posterior region, then much of the adaptation can occur during updates that are just finding the main posterior region, which can behave very differently that updates in the main region.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > HTH
> > > > > > > > > > -Perry
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 6:51 AM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > Good question, Rémi.  And I'm glad to hear you found the diagnostic information (scaleHistory, acceptanceRateHistory, etc) in the RW sampler to be helpful.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > At present, there's no such facilities in the slice sampler to record this history of the adaption process.  The slice sampler does adapt (every adaptInterval MCMC iterations), to modify the internal "width" variable, to make this "extension" width of the horizontal slice more suitable for the scale of the posterior distribution.  So, yes, tracking this "widthHistory" would be analogous to the adaptation history information in the RW sampler.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > At present, this information is not tracked in the slice sampler, but similar methods "getWidthHistory" could be added to the slice sampler.  I don't believe there are plans for adding it at the moment, but we would certainly welcome (and review) a pull-request to add this to the system.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > Short of that, modifying the sampler code and/or the nimble code base, you could also track this "width history" by extracting the "width" variable from the slice sampler after each MCMC iteration, making sure to set the nimble option:
> > > > > > > > > > > nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > This would work fine, and accomplish your goals.  A short example showing how to do that is below.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > Good luck with this,
> > > > > > > > > > > Daniel
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > library(nimble)
> > > > > > > > > > > nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > code <- nimbleCode({
> > > > > > > > > > >     a ~ dnorm(0, 1)
> > > > > > > > > > > })
> > > > > > > > > > > constants <- list()
> > > > > > > > > > > data <- list()
> > > > > > > > > > > inits <- list(a = 0)
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)
> > > > > > > > > > > Rmodel$calculate()
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, nodes = NULL)
> > > > > > > > > > > conf$addSampler('a', 'slice')
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
> > > > > > > > > > > Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > niter <- 10000
> > > > > > > > > > > set.seed(0)
> > > > > > > > > > > widthHistory <- numeric(niter)
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > for(i in 1:niter) {
> > > > > > > > > > >     Cmcmc$run(1, reset = (i==1))
> > > > > > > > > > >     widthHistory[i] <- Cmcmc$samplerFunctions[[1]]$width
> > > > > > > > > > > }
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > samples <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > plot(1:niter, widthHistory, type = 'l')
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 2:27 AM Rémi PATIN <remi...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > Hi all,

So I wanted to try other samplers (currently the slice) to see if it could ease the process and I was curious to see if there was a similar process during the adapatation phase for the slice samplers (but maybe you would have other suggestions for such cases).

> > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks in advance,

messages.body_plain:
With the graph it is better, sorry for the double post.
Rémi

On Tuesday, September 1, 2020 at 9:15:26 AM UTC+2 remi....@gmail.com wrote:
> Hi all,
> I have been trying to follow Daniel's suggestion of changing sampling order and I managed implementing these changes although results are mixed for now, but I still have many options to test concerning that (which nodes to resample, how many times should node be resampled...).However I had a question on how nimble worked and I wanted to be sure I was doing nothing wrong.
> Let's say I have 5 nodes A to E as in the graphs attach (it is a large simplification of a life cycle model with over 40 000 stochastic nodes)
> Node A, B, D are stochastic nodes while C and E are deterministic. C is calculated directly with the value of A and B. E depends on C and D.
> B is well mixed because its prior is very informative so its posterior distribution match very closely the prior.
> A and D are however poorly mixed compared to B and I wanted to improve model efficiency (in effective size/runtime). So instead of the default sample order (A,B,D), I wanted to try something like (A,B,D,A,B) so that each time D is sampled once, A and B are sampled twice, which should be increasing their effective sample size.
> I was wondering, between sampling of A and D, are the deterministic nodes updated? i.e., when the model samples variable D, is the value of node C updated according to the values in A ?
> Thanks in advance,
> Cheers,
> Rémi
>
> On Thursday, August 13, 2020 at 8:38:56 PM UTC+2 remi....@gmail.com wrote:
> > Wonderful, thank you very much for your help!
> > This may be quite rewardful in the end. I'll most definitely try that solution.
> >
> > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 7:26 PM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
> > > Yes.  Use the method (for example):
> > > conf$setSamplerExecutionOrder( c(1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) )
> > > or just as well:
> > > conf$setSamplerExecutionOrder( c(1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 4, 1, 5) )
> > >
> > > Also, then afterwards, you might find useful:
> > > conf$printSamplers(executionOrder = TRUE)
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 2:19 PM Rémi Patin <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Thanks a lot for the answer, that helps a lot.
> > > >
> > > > 1. Thank you, I will look into that to test it. Indeed that may be a niche issue to track acceptance without adaptation so I totally understand the choice.
> > > > I always thought that the model kept proposing a new sample until it was accepted before updating the other node so that's a great thing to know it is not the case! Thanks for highlighting the possibility to look into the posterior, I won't use it because I use thinning but that's good to know for the future.
> > > >
> > > > 2. Thanks for pointing me that idea, I will definitely want to try that.
> > > >
> > > > 3. If I understood correctly, at each iteration all nodes are updated but for some of them (56% based on the targeted 0.44 acceptance rate) the value stays the same because the proposal is refused. Is it possible to force more update on one node while other nodes are updated less frequently ? e.g. if node A is highly autocorrelated and have a poor mixing while node B has a good mixing, I would want node A to have a lower acceptance of proposal (therefore less autocorrelated) but to update until one proposal is accepted, before updating node B, so it would spare unneeded calculations on the update of node B, before node A finds a good proposal.
> > > >
> > > > Cheers,
> > > > Rémi
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > Le 13/08/2020 à 19:07, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > > > To answer your questions:
> > > > >
> > > > > 1. At present, when you specify adaptive=FALSE (thereby using a fixed proposal scale), the RW sampler doesn't record when / how often / the proportion of transitions (the acceptance rate).  And I'm hesitant to slow it down by tracking this, when it's non-adaptive.  That said, you could easily grab the code form GitHub
> > > > > https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/devel/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R#L165
> > > > > And modify it so that it still tracks this information even when adaptive=FALSE, but merely doesn't change the scale.  This could be done as easily as removing the one line:
> > > > > scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > > > > I'll put this modified code, below, and you would only have to remove the RW samplers that are assigned, and add (using conf$addSampler) the new "RW2" sampler, defined below.  To use this sampler, you would need to leave the default of adaptive=TRUE, and also set this nimble system option nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE).
> > > > >
> > > > > Another option would be for you to use the posterior samples calculate the RW acceptance rate, based on the proportion of times it successfully transitions (e.g., the parameter changes value).
> > > > >
> > > > > 2. About the target acceptance rate, right now it's hard-coded into the RW sampler at 0.44.  You can also change this in the code below, if you wish.  Or, if it's useful to you, I'm happy to change this into a (user-modifiable) "control list argument", with default value 0.44.  It would be a straightforward change to make, and could go into our next upcoming release (in a couple weeks).  Let me know if that sounds helpful.
> > > > >
> > > > > Cheers,
> > > > > Daniel
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > sampler_RW2 <- nimbleFunction(
> > > > >     name = 'sampler_RW2',
> > > > >     contains = sampler_BASE,
> > > > >     setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
> > > > >         ## control list extraction
> > > > >         logScale            <- if(!is.null(control$log))                 control$log                 else FALSE
> > > > >         reflective          <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))          control$reflective          else FALSE
> > > > >         adaptive            <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))            control$adaptive            else TRUE
> > > > >         adaptInterval       <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval))       control$adaptInterval       else 200
> > > > >         adaptFactorExponent <- if(!is.null(control$adaptFactorExponent)) control$adaptFactorExponent else 0.8
> > > > >         scale               <- if(!is.null(control$scale))               control$scale               else 1
> > > > >         ## node list generation
> > > > >         targetAsScalar <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
> > > > >         calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
> > > > >         calcNodesNoSelf <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE)
> > > > >         isStochCalcNodesNoSelf <- model$isStoch(calcNodesNoSelf)   ## should be made faster
> > > > >         calcNodesNoSelfDeterm <- calcNodesNoSelf[!isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > > > >         calcNodesNoSelfStoch <- calcNodesNoSelf[isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > > > >         ## numeric value generation
> > > > >         scaleOriginal <- scale
> > > > >         timesRan      <- 0
> > > > >         timesAccepted <- 0
> > > > >         timesAdapted  <- 0
> > > > >         scaleHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         acceptanceHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         if(nimbleOptions('MCMCsaveHistory')) {
> > > > >             saveMCMChistory <- TRUE
> > > > >         } else saveMCMChistory <- FALSE
> > > > >         optimalAR     <- 0.44
> > > > >         gamma1        <- 0
> > > > >         ## checks
> > > > >         if(length(targetAsScalar) > 1)   stop('cannot use RW sampler on more than one target; try RW_block sampler')
> > > > >         if(model$isDiscrete(target))     stop('cannot use RW sampler on discrete-valued target; try slice sampler')
> > > > >         if(logScale & reflective)        stop('cannot use reflective RW sampler on a log scale (i.e. with options log=TRUE and reflective=TRUE')
> > > > >         if(adaptFactorExponent < 0)      stop('cannot use RW sampler with adaptFactorExponent control parameter less than 0')
> > > > >         if(scale < 0)                    stop('cannot use RW sampler with scale control parameter less than 0')
> > > > >     },
> > > > >     run = function() {
> > > > >         currentValue <- model[[target]]
> > > > >         propLogScale <- 0
> > > > >         if(logScale) { propLogScale <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = scale)
> > > > >                        propValue <- currentValue * exp(propLogScale)
> > > > >         } else         propValue <- rnorm(1, mean = currentValue,  sd = scale)
> > > > >         if(reflective) {
> > > > >             lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> > > > >             upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> > > > >             while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
> > > > >                 if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
> > > > >                 if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
> > > > >             }
> > > > >         }
> > > > >         model[[target]] <<- propValue
> > > > >         logMHR <- calculateDiff(model, target)
> > > > >         if(logMHR == -Inf) {
> > > > >             nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > > >             ## Drawing a random number is needed during first testing
> > > > >             ## of this step in order to keep the random numbers identical
> > > > >             ## to old behavior to see if tests that depend on particular
> > > > >             ## sample sequences pass.  Rather than calling runif(1, 0, 1) here,
> > > > >             ## we call decide() to ensure same behavior.
> > > > >             ## jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > > > >             ## When new behavior is acceptable, we can remove the above line
> > > > >             ## and uncomment the following:
> > > > >             jump <- FALSE
> > > > >         } else {
> > > > >             logMHR <- logMHR + calculateDiff(model, calcNodesNoSelf) + propLogScale
> > > > >             jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > > > >             if(jump) {
> > > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > > > >             } else {
> > > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > > > >             }
> > > > >         }
> > > > >         if(adaptive)     adaptiveProcedure(jump)
> > > > >     },
> > > > >     methods = list(
> > > > >         adaptiveProcedure = function(jump = logical()) {
> > > > >             timesRan <<- timesRan + 1
> > > > >             if(jump)     timesAccepted <<- timesAccepted + 1
> > > > >             if(timesRan %% adaptInterval == 0) {
> > > > >                 acceptanceRate <- timesAccepted / timesRan
> > > > >                 timesAdapted <<- timesAdapted + 1
> > > > >                 if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > > >                     setSize(scaleHistory, timesAdapted)                 ## scaleHistory
> > > > >                     scaleHistory[timesAdapted] <<- scale                ## scaleHistory
> > > > >                     setSize(acceptanceHistory, timesAdapted)            ## scaleHistory
> > > > >                     acceptanceHistory[timesAdapted] <<- acceptanceRate  ## scaleHistory
> > > > >                 }
> > > > >                 gamma1 <<- 1/((timesAdapted + 3)^adaptFactorExponent)
> > > > >                 gamma2 <- 10 * gamma1
> > > > >                 adaptFactor <- exp(gamma2 * (acceptanceRate - optimalAR))
> > > > >                 ######scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > > > >                 ## If there are upper and lower bounds, enforce a maximum scale of
> > > > >                 ## 0.5 * (upper-lower).  This is arbitrary but reasonable.
> > > > >                 ## Otherwise, for a poorly-informed posterior,
> > > > >                 ## the scale could grow without bound to try to reduce
> > > > >                 ## acceptance probability.  This creates enormous cost of
> > > > >                 ## reflections.
> > > > >                 if(reflective) {
> > > > >                     lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> > > > >                     upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> > > > >                     if(scale >= 0.5*(upper-lower)) {
> > > > >                         scale <<- 0.5*(upper-lower)
> > > > >                     }
> > > > >                 }
> > > > >                 timesRan <<- 0
> > > > >                 timesAccepted <<- 0
> > > > >             }
> > > > >         },
> > > > >         getScaleHistory = function() {       ## scaleHistory
> > > > >             returnType(double(1))
> > > > >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > > >                 return(scaleHistory)
> > > > >             } else {
> > > > >                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
> > > > >                 return(numeric(1, 0))
> > > > >             }
> > > > >         },
> > > > >         getAcceptanceHistory = function() {  ## scaleHistory
> > > > >             returnType(double(1))
> > > > >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > > >                 return(acceptanceHistory)
> > > > >             } else {
> > > > >                 print("Please set 'nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE)' before building the MCMC")
> > > > >                 return(numeric(1, 0))
> > > > >             }
> > > > >         },
> > > > >         ##getScaleHistoryExpanded = function() {                                                 ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         ##    scaleHistoryExpanded <- numeric(timesAdapted*adaptInterval, init=FALSE)            ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         ##    for(iTA in 1:timesAdapted)                                                         ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         ##        for(j in 1:adaptInterval)                                                      ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         ##            scaleHistoryExpanded[(iTA-1)*adaptInterval+j] <- scaleHistory[iTA]         ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         ##    returnType(double(1)); return(scaleHistoryExpanded) },                             ## scaleHistory
> > > > >         reset = function() {
> > > > >             scale <<- scaleOriginal
> > > > >             timesRan      <<- 0
> > > > >             timesAccepted <<- 0
> > > > >             timesAdapted  <<- 0
> > > > >             if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > > >                 scaleHistory  <<- c(0, 0)    ## scaleHistory
> > > > >                 acceptanceHistory  <<- c(0, 0)
> > > > >             }
> > > > >             gamma1 <<- 0
> > > > >         }
> > > > >     )
> > > > > )
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > >
> > > > > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 12:56 PM Rémi Patin <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > I meant tracking the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler. Which from what I understood is still meaningful without adaptation for a sampler. Although it may be relatively constant, I would be interested by its level.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > However, I am also interested if you can make the RW sampler to tune itself towards another acceptance rate (right now it tunes toward something like 0.4 if I'm not mistaken)
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Le 13/08/2020 à 18:40, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > > > > > Thanks for following up, Rémi.   One question, when you say "would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate?", by the phrase "follow the acceptance rate", do you mean that the RW sampler itself tunes itself towards some "optimal" acceptance rate?  Or, do you mean for you to track (follow) the history of the acceptance rate of the sampler?
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > On Thu, Aug 13, 2020 at 10:40 AM remi....@gmail.com <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > Hi All,
> > > > > > > > Just a quick follow-up on the different solution I tested following Perry and Daniel advices:
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > - For following the adaptation phase of the slice sampler, I tested the manual solution of stopping the mcmc every 200 runs but it is quite time consuming to run through numerous samplers each time to get the `width` (it is still running in fact). I may test at some point the implementation I proposed in the dev version of nimble, but did not have time for it yet.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > - I also did some test by fixing the scale of the different RW samplers involved in the problematic nodes. Nothing conclusive for now. But I was wondering if it would be possible to use non-adaptive RW and still follow acceptance rate  ?
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > > Rémi
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > On Friday, July 31, 2020 at 5:04:21 PM UTC+2 pdevalpine wrote:
> > > > > > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > Sure that makes sense.  You could write a for loop to iterate over samplers for many nodes to set the proposal scale and turn the adapt flag FALSE for each one.  I suggested it because it sounded like you were conjecturing that the adaptation has not resulted in proposal scales that you think are most efficient.  (We usually think of efficiency in terms of (effective sample size) / computation time.  The computation time shouldn't change much or at all for different proposal scales, but the effective sample sizes almost certainly will.)  That is possible.  If you increase proposal scale, it may or may not increase effective sample size.  If it does, then fewer iterations would be needed.  I hope that helps.  Let us know if you get interesting results.
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > -Perry
> > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 7:48 AM Rémi PATIN <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > Hi Perry,
> > > > > > > > > > Thank you for the suggestion and the explanations to do it, I will give it a try. I am however a bit afraid to fix the RW proposal scale, because it concerns around ~2000 nodes. So I am not sure whether a single (or even a few) scale for all the nodes could do the trick.
> > > > > > > > > > I suppose if I manually fix the scale to higher value than produced by the adaptation phase, acceptation rate for those nodes will drop leading to slower iteration through those nodes. Meanwhile the samples should be less autocorrelated and less iterations would be needed ?
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > Concerning initial values, the model should have relatively good ones for most nodes. I know they have already worked on that and I think that we are currently using older model outputs to initiate the nodes in question. But I will keep that in mind, this could still be problematic.
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > Best,
> > > > > > > > > > Rémi
> > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > Le vendredi 31 juillet 2020 16:18:06 UTC+2, pdevalpine a écrit :
> > > > > > > > > > > Hi Rémi,
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > If you think the RW proposal scale has adapted to a value that is too small, I can give three suggestions for exploring the issue.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > 1. At the stage of the MCMC configuration (after configureMCMC) but before building the MCMC (before buildMCMC), find the relevant sampler by inspection of mcmcConf$printSamplers() or mcmcConf$getSamplers().  (Here mcmcConf is the object returned by configureMCMC).  Then modify the control list of that sampler to have adapt=FALSE and scale=<your choice>.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > 2. You can make the same settings by modifying the MCMC (after buildMCMC).  If you do it in the uncompiled version (before compileNimble), you can modify mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$scale and mcmc$samplerFunctions[[idx]]$adapt, where mcmc is the uncompiled MCMC.  Those values will then be copied to the compiled version to initialize it during compileNimble.  If you want to do it after compileNimble (with say Cmcmc instead of mcmc, where Cmcmc is the compiled version), you will need the same nimbleOptions setting Daniel provided.  You may want to do it this way because you could run it for a while, look at the scale value, then manually adjust it and continue running (with reset = FALSE) to experiment.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > 3. Sometimes providing good initial values can improve the outcome of the RW adaptation.  If the initial values are far from the main posterior region, then much of the adaptation can occur during updates that are just finding the main posterior region, which can behave very differently that updates in the main region.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > HTH
> > > > > > > > > > > -Perry
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > On Fri, Jul 31, 2020 at 6:51 AM Daniel Turek <db...@williams.edu> wrote:
> > > > > > > > > > > > Good question, Rémi.  And I'm glad to hear you found the diagnostic information (scaleHistory, acceptanceRateHistory, etc) in the RW sampler to be helpful.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > At present, there's no such facilities in the slice sampler to record this history of the adaption process.  The slice sampler does adapt (every adaptInterval MCMC iterations), to modify the internal "width" variable, to make this "extension" width of the horizontal slice more suitable for the scale of the posterior distribution.  So, yes, tracking this "widthHistory" would be analogous to the adaptation history information in the RW sampler.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > At present, this information is not tracked in the slice sampler, but similar methods "getWidthHistory" could be added to the slice sampler.  I don't believe there are plans for adding it at the moment, but we would certainly welcome (and review) a pull-request to add this to the system.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Short of that, modifying the sampler code and/or the nimble code base, you could also track this "width history" by extracting the "width" variable from the slice sampler after each MCMC iteration, making sure to set the nimble option:
> > > > > > > > > > > > nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > This would work fine, and accomplish your goals.  A short example showing how to do that is below.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Good luck with this,
> > > > > > > > > > > > Daniel
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > library(nimble)
> > > > > > > > > > > > nimbleOptions(buildInterfacesForCompiledNestedNimbleFunctions = TRUE)
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > code <- nimbleCode({
> > > > > > > > > > > >     a ~ dnorm(0, 1)
> > > > > > > > > > > > })
> > > > > > > > > > > > constants <- list()
> > > > > > > > > > > > data <- list()
> > > > > > > > > > > > inits <- list(a = 0)
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Rmodel <- nimbleModel(code, constants, data, inits)
> > > > > > > > > > > > Rmodel$calculate()
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > conf <- configureMCMC(Rmodel, nodes = NULL)
> > > > > > > > > > > > conf$addSampler('a', 'slice')
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Rmcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Cmodel <- compileNimble(Rmodel)
> > > > > > > > > > > > Cmcmc <- compileNimble(Rmcmc, project = Rmodel)

messages.body_plain:
Rémi, thanks for describing the situation well.  There's a chance I'm not understanding your question fully, but if I am, then:

After sampling any stochastic node, the deterministic nodes *which depend on the sampled node* are updated.  Any other deterministic nodes in the model are not updated, but that's because updating them would not change their value: the nodes they depend on did not change.

In your case, "i.e., when the model samples variable D, is the value of node C updated according to the values in A ?"  No, C is not updated, because it only depends on the values of A and B.  When the MCMC samples D, the value of D (only) might change.  Assuming the value of D changes, then it will recalculate E (since E depends on D), but not the value of C (since C does not depend on D, so even if we did "recalculate" C, the calculated value of C would be the same as before, since [after only updating D] the values of A and B are the same as before, so the re-calculation of C would be the same).

That said, after updating either A or B, then the value of C would be re-calculated using the updated value of (either) A or B, and then also the value of E would be re-calculated also using the updated value of C (and also using the un-changed value of D).

Does that make sense?  And answer your question?

Great job, and thank you for taking efforts to learn and understand how the system works.

Daniel

messages.body_plain:
Thank you again Daniel for the time you take answering such questions. This makes sense and fully answer my question!
Rémi

On Tuesday, September 1, 2020 at 4:10:11 PM UTC+2 db...@williams.edu wrote:
> Rémi, thanks for describing the situation well.  There's a chance I'm not understanding your question fully, but if I am, then:
>
> After sampling any stochastic node, the deterministic nodes *which depend on the sampled node* are updated.  Any other deterministic nodes in the model are not updated, but that's because updating them would not change their value: the nodes they depend on did not change.
>
> In your case, "i.e., when the model samples variable D, is the value of node C updated according to the values in A ?"  No, C is not updated, because it only depends on the values of A and B.  When the MCMC samples D, the value of D (only) might change.  Assuming the value of D changes, then it will recalculate E (since E depends on D), but not the value of C (since C does not depend on D, so even if we did "recalculate" C, the calculated value of C would be the same as before, since [after only updating D] the values of A and B are the same as before, so the re-calculation of C would be the same).
>
> That said, after updating either A or B, then the value of C would be re-calculated using the updated value of (either) A or B, and then also the value of E would be re-calculated also using the updated value of C (and also using the un-changed value of D).
>
> Does that make sense?  And answer your question?
>
> Great job, and thank you for taking efforts to learn and understand how the system works.
>
> Daniel
>
>
> On Tue, Sep 1, 2020 at 3:18 AM remi....@gmail.com <remi....@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > Let's say I have 5 nodes A to E as in the graphs attach (it is a large simplification of a life cycle model with over 40 000 stochastic nodes)
> > > Node A, B, D are stochastic nodes while C and E are deterministic. C is calculated directly with the value of A and B. E depends on C and D.
> > > B is well mixed because its prior is very informative so its posterior distribution match very closely the prior.
> > > A and D are however poorly mixed compared to B and I wanted to improve model efficiency (in effective size/runtime). So instead of the default sample order (A,B,D), I wanted to try something like (A,B,D,A,B) so that each time D is sampled once, A and B are sampled twice, which should be increasing their effective sample size.
> > > I was wondering, between sampling of A and D, are the deterministic nodes updated? i.e., when the model samples variable D, is the value of node C updated according to the values in A ?

> > > > > > Thanks a lot for the answer, that helps a lot.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 1. Thank you, I will look into that to test it. Indeed that may be a niche issue to track acceptance without adaptation so I totally understand the choice.
> > > > > > I always thought that the model kept proposing a new sample until it was accepted before updating the other node so that's a great thing to know it is not the case! Thanks for highlighting the possibility to look into the posterior, I won't use it because I use thinning but that's good to know for the future.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > 2. Thanks for pointing me that idea, I will definitely want to try that.

If I understood correctly, at each iteration all nodes are updated but for some of them (56% based on the targeted 0.44 acceptance rate) the value stays the same because the proposal is refused. Is it possible to force more update on one node while other nodes are updated less frequently ? e.g. if node A is highly autocorrelated and have a poor mixing while node B has a good mixing, I would want node A to have a lower acceptance of proposal (therefore less autocorrelated) but to update until one proposal is accepted, before updating node B, so it would spare unneeded calculations on the update of node B, before node A finds a good proposal.

> > > > > > Le 13/08/2020 à 19:07, Daniel Turek a écrit :
> > > > > > > To answer your questions:
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 1. At present, when you specify adaptive=FALSE (thereby using a fixed proposal scale), the RW sampler doesn't record when / how often / the proportion of transitions (the acceptance rate).  And I'm hesitant to slow it down by tracking this, when it's non-adaptive.  That said, you could easily grab the code form GitHub
> > > > > > > https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/blob/devel/packages/nimble/R/MCMC_samplers.R#L165
> > > > > > > And modify it so that it still tracks this information even when adaptive=FALSE, but merely doesn't change the scale.  This could be done as easily as removing the one line:
> > > > > > > scale <<- scale * adaptFactor
> > > > > > > I'll put this modified code, below, and you would only have to remove the RW samplers that are assigned, and add (using conf$addSampler) the new "RW2" sampler, defined below.  To use this sampler, you would need to leave the default of adaptive=TRUE, and also set this nimble system option nimbleOptions(MCMCsaveHistory = TRUE).
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Another option would be for you to use the posterior samples calculate the RW acceptance rate, based on the proportion of times it successfully transitions (e.g., the parameter changes value).
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > 2. About the target acceptance rate, right now it's hard-coded into the RW sampler at 0.44.  You can also change this in the code below, if you wish.  Or, if it's useful to you, I'm happy to change this into a (user-modifiable) "control list argument", with default value 0.44.  It would be a straightforward change to make, and could go into our next upcoming release (in a couple weeks).  Let me know if that sounds helpful.
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > Cheers,
> > > > > > > Daniel
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > >
> > > > > > > sampler_RW2 <- nimbleFunction(
> > > > > > >     name = 'sampler_RW2',
> > > > > > >     contains = sampler_BASE,
> > > > > > >     setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
> > > > > > >         ## control list extraction
> > > > > > >         logScale            <- if(!is.null(control$log))                 control$log                 else FALSE
> > > > > > >         reflective          <- if(!is.null(control$reflective))          control$reflective          else FALSE
> > > > > > >         adaptive            <- if(!is.null(control$adaptive))            control$adaptive            else TRUE
> > > > > > >         adaptInterval       <- if(!is.null(control$adaptInterval))       control$adaptInterval       else 200
> > > > > > >         adaptFactorExponent <- if(!is.null(control$adaptFactorExponent)) control$adaptFactorExponent else 0.8
> > > > > > >         scale               <- if(!is.null(control$scale))               control$scale               else 1
> > > > > > >         ## node list generation
> > > > > > >         targetAsScalar <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
> > > > > > >         calcNodes <- model$getDependencies(target)
> > > > > > >         calcNodesNoSelf <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE)
> > > > > > >         isStochCalcNodesNoSelf <- model$isStoch(calcNodesNoSelf)   ## should be made faster
> > > > > > >         calcNodesNoSelfDeterm <- calcNodesNoSelf[!isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > > > > > >         calcNodesNoSelfStoch <- calcNodesNoSelf[isStochCalcNodesNoSelf]
> > > > > > >         ## numeric value generation
> > > > > > >         scaleOriginal <- scale
> > > > > > >         timesRan      <- 0
> > > > > > >         timesAccepted <- 0
> > > > > > >         timesAdapted  <- 0
> > > > > > >         scaleHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > > > > > >         acceptanceHistory  <- c(0, 0)   ## scaleHistory
> > > > > > >         if(nimbleOptions('MCMCsaveHistory')) {
> > > > > > >             saveMCMChistory <- TRUE
> > > > > > >         } else saveMCMChistory <- FALSE
> > > > > > >         optimalAR     <- 0.44
> > > > > > >         gamma1        <- 0
> > > > > > >         ## checks
> > > > > > >         if(length(targetAsScalar) > 1)   stop('cannot use RW sampler on more than one target; try RW_block sampler')
> > > > > > >         if(model$isDiscrete(target))     stop('cannot use RW sampler on discrete-valued target; try slice sampler')
> > > > > > >         if(logScale & reflective)        stop('cannot use reflective RW sampler on a log scale (i.e. with options log=TRUE and reflective=TRUE')
> > > > > > >         if(adaptFactorExponent < 0)      stop('cannot use RW sampler with adaptFactorExponent control parameter less than 0')
> > > > > > >         if(scale < 0)                    stop('cannot use RW sampler with scale control parameter less than 0')
> > > > > > >     },
> > > > > > >     run = function() {
> > > > > > >         currentValue <- model[[target]]
> > > > > > >         propLogScale <- 0
> > > > > > >         if(logScale) { propLogScale <- rnorm(1, mean = 0, sd = scale)
> > > > > > >                        propValue <- currentValue * exp(propLogScale)
> > > > > > >         } else         propValue <- rnorm(1, mean = currentValue,  sd = scale)
> > > > > > >         if(reflective) {
> > > > > > >             lower <- model$getBound(target, 'lower')
> > > > > > >             upper <- model$getBound(target, 'upper')
> > > > > > >             while(propValue < lower | propValue > upper) {
> > > > > > >                 if(propValue < lower) propValue <- 2*lower - propValue
> > > > > > >                 if(propValue > upper) propValue <- 2*upper - propValue
> > > > > > >             }
> > > > > > >         }
> > > > > > >         model[[target]] <<- propValue
> > > > > > >         logMHR <- calculateDiff(model, target)
> > > > > > >         if(logMHR == -Inf) {
> > > > > > >             nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > > > > >             ## Drawing a random number is needed during first testing
> > > > > > >             ## of this step in order to keep the random numbers identical
> > > > > > >             ## to old behavior to see if tests that depend on particular
> > > > > > >             ## sample sequences pass.  Rather than calling runif(1, 0, 1) here,
> > > > > > >             ## we call decide() to ensure same behavior.
> > > > > > >             ## jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > > > > > >             ## When new behavior is acceptable, we can remove the above line
> > > > > > >             ## and uncomment the following:
> > > > > > >             jump <- FALSE
> > > > > > >         } else {
> > > > > > >             logMHR <- logMHR + calculateDiff(model, calcNodesNoSelf) + propLogScale
> > > > > > >             jump <- decide(logMHR)
> > > > > > >             if(jump) {
> > > > > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > > > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > > > > > >                 nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > > > > > >             } else {
> > > > > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
> > > > > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfDeterm, logProb = FALSE)
> > > > > > >                 nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = calcNodesNoSelfStoch, logProbOnly = TRUE)
> > > > > > >             }
> > > > > > >         }
> > > > > > >         if(adaptive)     adaptiveProcedure(jump)
> > > > > > >     },
> > > > > > >     methods = list(
> > > > > > >         adaptiveProcedure = function(jump = logical()) {
> > > > > > >             timesRan <<- timesRan + 1
> > > > > > >             if(jump)     timesAccepted <<- timesAccepted + 1
> > > > > > >             if(timesRan %% adaptInterval == 0) {
> > > > > > >                 acceptanceRate <- timesAccepted / timesRan
> > > > > > >                 timesAdapted <<- timesAdapted + 1
> > > > > > >                 if(saveMCMChistory) {
> > > > > > >                     setSize(scaleHistory, timesAdapted)                 ## scaleHistory
> > > > > > >                     scaleHistory[timesAdapted] <<- scale                ## scaleHistory
> > > > > > >                     setSize(acceptanceHistory, timesAdapted)            ## scaleHistory
> > > > > > >                     acceptanceHistory[timesAdapted] <<- acceptanceRate  ## scaleHistory
> > > > > > >                 }
> > > > > > >                 gamma1 <<- 1/((timesAdapted + 3)^adaptFactorExponent)
> > > > > > >                 gamma2 <- 10 * gamma1
> > > > > > >                 adaptFactor <- exp(gamma2 * (acceptanceRate - optimalAR))

Hi Andrew,

Thanks for the query and sorry for the slow response time.  Your message got unlucky and lost the lottery of nimble developer availability ;-)

I think the foldCVstandardError uses a batch means method (or moving block bootstrap) to estimate the Monte Carlo error in the cross-validation prediction error for each fold.  Getting these error estimates is not necessary to make use of cross validation, but it can be informative.  I agree it is suspicious for it to be zero in every fold (or any fold).  That might reflect that the MCMC for each fold is not mixing.  Can you try using returnSamples = TRUE to check on whether the samples are mixing?  From reading your code, I am not seeing what the problem might be.  If you would be able to reduce your model to a simple toy and still reproduce the problem and send that along as a minimal reproducible example, that would be very helpful for us to investigate.  Thanks.

-Perry

> Hello,
>
> After accounting for spatial autocorrelation in various community N-mixture models estimated, I am currently using runCrossValidate( ) to conduct k-fold cross-validation to select between candidate models. As Hooten and Hobbs (2015) note, WAIC is not recommended for use in model selection when considering models that incorporate correlated error structures (e.g., spatial [conditional autoregressive] terms); hence, I am using cross-validation with a loss function, instead.
>
> With the help of the user manual, I incorporated a loss function (i.e. RMSE) into runCrossValidate( ):
> {
> # Define the fold function
> commNmix_FoldFunction <- function(i) {
>   foldNodes_i <- paste0('Yc[', i, ', , ]')  # Will return 'Yc[1 , , ]' for i = 1 (e.g., based on nsite)
>   return(foldNodes_i)
> }
>
> # Define the loss function
> RMSE_lossFunction <- function(simulatedDataValues, actualDataValues) {
>   dataLength <- length(simulatedDataValues) # simulatedDataValues is a vector
>   SSE <- 0
>
>   for(i in 1:dataLength){
>     SSE <- SSE + (simulatedDataValues[i] - actualDataValues[i])^2
>   }
>
>   MSE <- SSE / dataLength
>   RMSE <- sqrt(MSE)
>   return(RMSE)
> }
>
> commNmix_MCMCconfiguration <- configureMCMC(Rmodel)

> crossValOutput <- runCrossValidate(MCMCconfiguration = commNmix_MCMCconfiguration,

Hi Perry et al.,

Today, I am taking a look at two different sets of MCMC samples from my preliminary cross-validation approach.

For the first set (i.e. folding over sites or spatial replicates):
{

# Define the fold function
commNmix_FoldFunction <- function(i) {
  foldNodes_i <- paste0('Yc[ ', i, ', , ]')  # Will return 'Yc[1 , , ]' for i = 1 (e.g., based on nsite)
  return(foldNodes_i)

  }
}

For the second set (i.e. folding over site visits or temporal replicates):
{

# Define the fold function
commNmix_FoldFunction <- function(i) {

  foldNodes_i <- paste0('Yc[ , ', i, ' , ]')  # Will return 'Yc[, 1 , ]' for i = 1 (e.g., based on nrep)
  return(foldNodes_i)
  }
}

For viewing cross-validation information with an actual model, here is code for a candidate model (i.e. which does exhibit mixed chains following completion):

codeFbGs <- nimbleCode({

  # Community priors (with hyperparameters) for species-specific parameters
  for(k in 1:nspec){
    phi[k] ~ dunif(0, 1)                                                                                  # adjustment for zero-inflation

    # Alpha parameters (detection)
    alpha0[k] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha0, sd=sd.alpha0)                                  # intercept on detection
    alpha1[k] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha1, sd=sd.alpha1)                                  # linear julian day on detection
    alpha2[k] ~ dnorm(mu.alpha2, sd=sd.alpha2)                                  # quadratic julian day on detection

    # Beta Parameters (abundance)
    for(s in 1:nyear){
      beta0[k,s] ~ dnorm(mu.beta0[s], sd=sd.beta0[s])                           # year-specific intercept on abundance
    }
    beta1[k] ~ dnorm(mu.beta1, sd=sd.beta1)                                        # treatment type (dummy coded)
    beta2[k] ~ dnorm(mu.beta2, sd=sd.beta2)                                        # percent forb cover
    beta3[k] ~ dnorm(mu.beta3, sd=sd.beta3)                                        # percent grass cover
  }

  # Hyperpriors for community hyperparameters
  # abundance model
  for(s in 1:nyear){
    mu.beta0[s] ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
    sd.beta0[s] ~ dunif(0, 10)
  }
  mu.beta1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
  sd.beta1 ~ dunif(0, 10)
  mu.beta2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
  sd.beta2 ~ dunif(0, 10)
  mu.beta3 ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
  sd.beta3 ~ dunif(0, 10)

  # detection model
  mu.alpha0 ~ dnorm(mu.a0L, sd.alpha0)
  sd.alpha0 ~ dunif(0, 1)
  mu.a0 ~ dunif(0, 1)
  mu.a0L <- logit(mu.a0)
  mu.alpha1 ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
  sd.alpha1 ~ dunif(0, 10)
  mu.alpha2 ~ dnorm(0, 0.01)
  sd.alpha2 ~ dunif(0, 10)

  #Conditional autoregressive process (e.g., spatial random fields)
  tau.w ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
  for(i in 1:L){
    weights[i] <- 1
    W[1:ncar] ~ dcar_normal(adj[1:L], weights[1:L], num[1:ncar], tau.w, zero_mean=1)
    W2[1:nsite] <- c(W[1:ncar], W[1:ncar])
  }

  # Ecological model for true abundance (process model)
  for(k in 1:nspec){
    for(i in 1:nsite){
      a[i,k] ~ dbern(phi[k])                                                    # adjustment for zero-inflation
      N[i,k] ~ dpois(a[i,k] * lambda[i,k])
      log(lambda[i,k]) <- beta0[k, year[i]] + beta1[k] * Treatment[i] + beta2[k] * PercForb[i] +
        beta3[k] * PercGrass[i] + W2[i]

      # Compute presence/absence matrix z (for N > 0) from latent abundance
      z[i,k] <- step(N[i,k]-1)  # returns TRUE if N >= 0
    }
  }

  #Complex (community) beta-binomial specification
  tau <- exp(tau.log)
  tau.log ~ dnorm(0, 1)

  # Observation model for replicated counts
  for(k in 1:nspec){
    for(i in 1:nsite){
      for(j in 1:nrep){
        Yc[i,j,k] ~ dbin(p[i,j,k], N[i,k])
        p[i,j,k] ~ T(dbeta(tau*mu[i,j,k], tau*(1-mu[i,j,k])), 0.001, 0.999)
        logit(mu[i,j,k]) <- alpha0[k] + alpha1[k] * JulianDay[i] + alpha2[k] * pow(JulianDay[i], 2)
      }
    }
  }

  # Other derived quantities
  for(k in 1:nspec){
    for(s in 1:nyear){
      mlambda[k,s] <- phi[k] * exp(beta0[k,s])                                  # Expected abundance on natural scale
      logit(mp[k]) <- alpha0[k]                                                            # Mean detection on natural scale
    }
    Nocc.fs[k] <- sum(z[1:nsite,k])                                                   # Number of occupied sites among the 28
  }

    Nbirds[i] <- sum(N[i,1:nspec])                                                   # Number of total individuals at each site
  }
})

I am new to nimble, so I suspect that I just doing something wrong, but I cannot spot the problem. Hopefully it is so obvious that its easily spotted by more experienced users.

In brief, I setup a model and it runs fine with nimbleMCMC using the default samplers. Because this is a state space model I would like to use RW_PF_block. But when I do this I get Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors.

My model comes with quite a bit of baggage. I have made a portable version of the problem. This mimics the structure that I have used and reproduces the error. The error message is rather generic though and does not help me.

pasted below is a portable version of the problem/mistake.

rm(list=ls())
library(nimble)

# make some data
n <- 100 # number of data points
t <- seq(0,4*pi,,100)
a <- 3
b <- 2
amp <- 2
vi <- a*sin(b*t)+rnorm(n)*amp
TAIR <- a*sin(b*t)+rnorm(n)*amp

input.data = list(TAIR = TAIR)
input.data$lo <- rep(0,7)
input.data$up <- rep(1,7)
input.data$mu <- input.data$up - input.data$lo
input.data$steps <- n

inits.data = list(parset=runif(2,0,1))
inits.data$sdb <- 0.01
inits.data$sdp <- 0.01
inits.data$sdo <- 0.01
inits.data$m <- 1.0
inits.data$zstart <- 0.5

resp.data <- list(vi = vi)

ttrTimeNimble <- nimbleCode({

    for(i in 1: 2) {
     parset[i] ~ T( dnorm( mu[i], sdb), lo[i], up[i] )
     }

     sdp ~ dunif(lo[3], up[3])       # process error
     sdo ~ dunif(lo[4], up[4])       # observation error
     sdb ~ dunif(lo[6], up[6])
     zstart ~ T( dnorm(mu[5],sd=sdp),lo[5], up[5])
     m ~ T(dnorm(mu[7],sd=0.5),lo[7],)

     z[1] <- zstart
     vi[1] ~ dnorm(z[1]*m,sd=sdo)

    for (i in 2:steps) {
        zz[i] <- TAIR[i]*parset[1] + parset[2]
        z[i] ~  dnorm(zz[i],  sd = sdp)
        vi[i] ~ dnorm(z[i]*m, sd = sdo)
    }

})

ttrTimeModel <- nimbleModel(code = ttrTimeNimble, constants = input.data,
                            data = resp.data, inits = inits.data)
mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(code = ttrTimeNimble, constants = input.data,
                       data = resp.data, inits = inits.data,
                       nchains = 3, niter = 500,
                       summary = TRUE, WAIC = FALSE,
                       monitors = c('parset','m','sdo', 'sdp','sdb','zstart'))

#--now specify a particle filter
CttrTimeModel <- compileNimble(ttrTimeModel)
ttrTimeConf <- configureMCMC(ttrTimeModel, nodes = NULL,
                              monitors = c('parset','m','sdo', 'sdp','sdb','zstart'))
dd<-rep(1,7)
ttrTimeConf$addSampler(target = c('parset','m','sdo', 'sdp','sdb','zstart'),
                            type = 'RW_PF_block',
                            control = list(propCov = diag(dd),
                                           adaptScaleOnly = FALSE,
                                           latents = "z", pfOptimizeNparticles = TRUE
                                      ))

ttrTimeMCMC <- buildMCMC(ttrTimeModel)
# no error, but this is not using ttrTimeConf
ttrTimeMCMC <- buildMCMC(ttrTimeConf,resetFunctions=TRUE)
#Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
ttrTimeMCMC <- buildMCMC(ttrTimeConf)
#Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

many thanks in advance
Steve

messages.body_plain:
Indeed, most unfortunately this comes down to an issue with R, and "partial matching" of list names.  The problem can be summarized by the following simplified example of the same problem:

myList <- list(longName = 5)
myList$longName  ## returns 5, which is correct
myList$long      ## also returns 5, which is not really correct....

In your case, the control list element that you're providing "pfOptimizeNparticles = TRUE" is unfortunately being "partially matched" by extraction of the alternate control list element named "pf", by the code "control$pf", and hence the RW_PF_block is using TRUE for the "pf" control list element, and also using TRUE for "pfOptimizeNparticles" element (as was intended).  This isn't an error in the sampler, per se, but rather a problem in how NIMBLE's MCMC samplers process control list elements - in particular those which "partially match" the names of other control list elements.

In short - this is a problem on our end.  And it will be addressed.

In the meantime, a workaround is provided below, where I also provide the default value (NULL) for the "pf" control list element, and now it should work fine for you.

Thanks for raising this.

Daniel

ttrTimeConf$addSampler(target = c('parset','m','sdo', 'sdp','sdb','zstart'),
                       type = 'RW_PF_block',
                       control = list(
                           propCov = diag(dd),
                           adaptScaleOnly = FALSE,
                           latents = "z",

                           pf = NULL,       ## this line is new
                           pfOptimizeNparticles = TRUE))

> A set of nimble functions for adaptive parallel tempering are available in a small library called NimbleSnippets available here <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1049549>. The source code can be built into an R package and installed using
> cd path/to/nimble-snippets
> R CMD build nimble-snippets
> R CMD INSTALL NimbleSnippets_1.0.1.tar.gz
>
> Feel free to contact me if you have any difficulties, or successes, with the package.
>
> Best
> David
>

On Thursday, 3 September 2020 at 21:34:11 UTC+2 db...@williams.edu wrote:
> Indeed, most unfortunately this comes down to an issue with R, and "partial matching" of list names.  The problem can be summarized by the following simplified example of the same problem:
>
> myList <- list(longName = 5)
> myList$longName  ## returns 5, which is correct
> myList$long      ## also returns 5, which is not really correct....
>
> In your case, the control list element that you're providing "pfOptimizeNparticles = TRUE" is unfortunately being "partially matched" by extraction of the alternate control list element named "pf", by the code "control$pf", and hence the RW_PF_block is using TRUE for the "pf" control list element, and also using TRUE for "pfOptimizeNparticles" element (as was intended).  This isn't an error in the sampler, per se, but rather a problem in how NIMBLE's MCMC samplers process control list elements - in particular those which "partially match" the names of other control list elements.
>
> In short - this is a problem on our end.  And it will be addressed.
>
> In the meantime, a workaround is provided below, where I also provide the default value (NULL) for the "pf" control list element, and now it should work fine for you.
>
> Thanks for raising this.
>
> Daniel
>
>
> ttrTimeConf$addSampler(target = c('parset','m','sdo', 'sdp','sdb','zstart'),
>                        type = 'RW_PF_block',
>                        control = list(
>                            propCov = diag(dd),
>                            adaptScaleOnly = FALSE,
>                            latents = "z",
>                            pf = NULL,       ## this line is new
>                            pfOptimizeNparticles = TRUE))
>

> >

> >
> > input.data = list(TAIR = TAIR)
> > input.data$lo <- rep(0,7)
> > input.data$up <- rep(1,7)
> > input.data$mu <- input.data$up - input.data$lo
> > input.data$steps <- n
> >
> > inits.data = list(parset=runif(2,0,1))
> > inits.data$sdb <- 0.01
> > inits.data$sdp <- 0.01
> > inits.data$sdo <- 0.01
> > inits.data$m <- 1.0
> > inits.data$zstart <- 0.5
> >
> > resp.data <- list(vi = vi)
> >
> > ttrTimeNimble <- nimbleCode({
> >
> >     for(i in 1: 2) {
> >      parset[i] ~ T( dnorm( mu[i], sdb), lo[i], up[i] )
> >      }
> >
> >      sdp ~ dunif(lo[3], up[3])       # process error
> >      sdo ~ dunif(lo[4], up[4])       # observation error
> >      sdb ~ dunif(lo[6], up[6])

messages.body_plain:
To provide additional information to this thread, I should also note that recent compilation of the example code for the 'runCrossValidate( )' function (i.e. using the 'dyesData' here <https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/nimble/versions/0.9.1/topics/runCrossValidate>) shows that it returns CV standard errors of 0 in its 'crossValOutput' list as well. This suggests to me that the issue may not be related to my community N-mixture model or its input data, but perhaps related to either example- or source-code operations, instead.

Best,
Andrew

messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,

Thanks for being patient on this.  There is indeed a bug in cross validation that was an inadvertent (and untrapped) consequence of a change in other code.  Thanks for your efforts in identifying the problem.

In a day or two we'll have a fix in our development version on GitHub.  That can always be installed by

library(devtools)
install_github("nimble-dev/nimble", ref = "devel", subdir = "packages/nimble")

I'll send another note on this thread to confirm when the bug fix is there.  It will also go into an upcoming release fairly soon.

-Perry

On Fri, Sep 4, 2020 at 1:22 PM Andrew <ajden...@gmail.com> wrote:

> To provide additional information to this thread, I should also note that recent compilation of the example code for the 'runCrossValidate( )' function (i.e. using the 'dyesData' here <https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/nimble/versions/0.9.1/topics/runCrossValidate>) shows that it returns CV standard errors of 0 in its 'crossValOutput' list as well. This suggests to me that the issue may not be related to my community N-mixture model or its input data, but perhaps related to either example- or source-code operations, instead.
>
> Best,
> Andrew
>
> On Wednesday, September 2, 2020 at 3:58:19 PM UTC-4 Andrew wrote:
> > Hi Perry et al.,
> >
> > Today, I am taking a look at two different sets of MCMC samples from my preliminary cross-validation approach.
> >

> >   return(foldNodes_i)
> >   }
> > }
> >
> > For the first set, MCMC samples return the same values of y in each row per fold, as the folds occur over sites. This must be the culprit behind estimated standard errors = 0 per fold.
> >
> > For example, here is a subset of cross-validation y samples from just one fold, based on the first set's fold function (i.e. for each i th site, j th visit, and k th species in Yc[ i , j , k], returned by crossValOutput$samples[ [ 1 ] ] ):

> >    [13,]           8           1           4           0           0           0           4           1
> >    [14,]           8           1           4           0           0           0           4           1

> >
> > I am still waiting to see what the second set, folding over site visits, returns later today.
> >
> > For viewing cross-validation information with an actual model, here is code for a candidate model (i.e. which does exhibit mixed chains following completion):
> > {
> > codeFbGs <- nimbleCode({
> >
> >   # Community priors (with hyperparameters) for species-specific parameters

> >   }
> >
> >   # Hyperpriors for community hyperparameters

> >   # Ecological model for true abundance (process model)

> > })
> >
> > nyear <- length(c(2005,2006))
> > nsite <- dim(Ycd)[1]
